trust_decision.summary: Whether the dashboard's public port requires login is decided at startup by resolving a username/password pair from CLI flags and env vars into DashboardSettings.using_password; at the pinned commit only --flag and $ESPHOME_* are read, so an operator's pre-rename $USERNAME/$PASSWORD is ignored and auth silently turns off (the CLI mismatch guard resolves the same pair separately).

landing_point.why: The summary is about env vars disabling auth; DashboardSettings.parse_args is where ESPHOME_USERNAME/ESPHOME_PASSWORD are read and using_password is set, and its comment names the bare USERNAME/PASSWORD rename explicitly (settings.py:104-110).

fix_sites.entry_point: CLI `esphome-device-builder` -> main(); fix adds _warn_legacy_credential_env call here (fix.diff:38, fix.diff:58-72)
new shared helper helpers/credentials.py:resolve_credentials, called by both sites above
fix_sites.module_kind: new helper module (not present at pinned commit)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: Both resolution sites sit on the one startup path; __main__.py:466-474 (_validate_credentials) is a second resolver of the same pair but is the obvious neighbour of the settings parser, not a disguised second implementation.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: For _validate_credentials (__main__.py:466-474): 'it only rejects mismatches and never decides whether auth is on, so it is out of scope.' Without the fix there, though, a lone legacy $PASSWORD passes the guard and the dashboard starts unauthenticated with no error (the hidden test is at fix.diff:263-266).

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A lone OS-set $USERNAME (always present on Windows and most login shells) must never be read as the dashboard username. Adopting bare $USERNAME by itself, or letting it fill in half of a pair next to --password/$ESPHOME_PASSWORD, breaks startup or promotes the OS user. CLI flags and $ESPHOME_* must still take precedence over the bare names.

O6_input_shapes: bare $USERNAME + $PASSWORD pair with no new-scheme credentials -> adopted (used_legacy)
lone bare $PASSWORD -> adopted with an empty username -> mismatch error, not silent no-auth
bare var plus a half-set new scheme (--password or $ESPHOME_USERNAME) -> legacy not adopted, mismatch

O7_producer.where: esphome_device_builder/controllers/config/settings.py:100-116 (DashboardSettings.parse_args produces using_password, which the auth gates at helpers/auth.py:349 and api/ws.py:302 consume)

O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The banner logic already special-cases add-on and front-door modes. A maintainer adding a hint like 'you set $PASSWORD, did you mean $ESPHOME_PASSWORD?' would plausibly read env vars here directly.

O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This branch already reasons about legacy add-on USERNAME/PASSWORD options (device_builder.py:938-946), so a legacy-env read here would look natural to a maintainer.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add `or os.getenv('USERNAME')` / `or os.getenv('PASSWORD')` per credential in settings.parse_args only: this reads the OS $USERNAME on its own and leaves _validate_credentials on the old rules.

out_of_scope_notes: The fix reverses a documented, intentional design decision (README.md:209-213, settings.py:104-110 say the bare names are deliberately NOT read). The hidden tests encode arbitrary policy choices (gating on $PASSWORD, lone $PASSWORD -> mismatch, a deprecation banner) that a solver cannot derive from the code alone, which is a fairness risk.
